title: High-dimensional inference for the $γ$-ray sky with differentiable programming
summary: We motivate the use of differentiable probabilistic programming techniques in order to account for the large model-space inherent to astrophysical $γ$-ray analyses. Targeting the longstanding Galactic Center $γ$-ray Excess (GCE) puzzle, we construct differentiable forward model and likelihood that make liberal use of GPU acceleration and vectorization in order to simultaneously account for a continuum of possible spatial morphologies consistent with the GCE emission in a fully probabilistic manner. Our setup allows for efficient inference over the large model space using variational methods. Beyond application to $γ$-ray data, a goal of this work is to showcase how differentiable probabilistic programming can be used as a tool to enable flexible analyses of astrophysical datasets.

AI.tldr: This paper applies differentiable probabilistic programming with GPU acceleration to model the Galactic Center gamma-ray Excess, enabling efficient, flexible probabilistic inference over complex astrophysical data.
AI.motivation: Address the complex, large model space in astrophysical gamma-ray analyses, specifically the Galactic Center gamma-ray Excess (GCE) puzzle.
AI.method: Develop a differentiable forward model and likelihood leveraging GPU acceleration and vectorization, allowing for probabilistic modeling of a continuum of spatial morphologies; perform efficient inference using variational methods.
AI.result: Established a framework capable of fully probabilistic inference over a large model space related to GCE emission, demonstrating computational efficiency and flexibility.
AI.conclusion: Differentiable probabilistic programming enables flexible and efficient analyses of complex astrophysical gamma-ray datasets, exemplified by application to the GCE puzzle, supporting advanced model-space exploration.

title: Ghosts of eruptions past: Searching for historical Galactic supernovae using variable thermal dust echoes and machine learning
comment: 10 pages, 6 figures (+ 3 pages, 4 figures in Appendix). Submitted to ApJ. Comments welcome!
summary: The Galactic core-collapse supernova (SN) rate is estimated at $\approx 1-3$ per century; however, no optically visible SN has been discovered in the past 400 years. Although records of the last optically detected SN (Cassiopeia A) are debated, it is revealed today via its bright, variable mid-infrared (MIR) dust echoes -- offering the possibility of identifying dust-obscured, missed events via their dust echoes. We present the first all-sky, untargeted search for thermal dust echoes of luminous Galactic transients using difference imaging on 12 years of time-resolved NEOWISE co-adds (spanning $2009-2022$) followed by statistical detection of variable extended sources. We use echo features around Cas A, together with archival catalogs to train a convolutional neural network to classify transient candidates as dust echoes, point sources, artifacts, and high proper motion stars. Our model achieves $\approx 94$% accuracy in distinguishing echoes from other variable sources. Applying the classifier to $\approx 11$ million transient candidates, we search for spatial over-densities of echoes across the Galactic plane. We find that Cas A is the only region exhibiting echoes at the WISE sensitivity threshold of $W2$ surface brightness of $\approx 20$ Vega mag arcsec$^{-2}$ -- reflecting its unique combination of young age and luminous shock breakout. We present the largest catalog of time-resolved echo positions of Cas A (20477 within 10$^\circ$) that are being used for studies of the surrounding interstellar medium with the James Webb Space Telescope. Our results lay the groundwork for the imminent Roman space telescope surveys -- which will achieve $\approx 100\times$ higher sensitivity and $\approx 30\times$ better spatial resolution at wavelengths of $\lesssim 2.5\,μ$m.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the first all-sky search for Galactic supernova dust echoes using 12 years of NEOWISE mid-infrared data and machine learning. They achieve high classification accuracy, find only Cassiopeia A exhibiting echoes at current sensitivity, and compile a large echo catalog for further study, paving the way for advanced future surveys.
AI.motivation: There is a discrepancy between the expected Galactic core-collapse supernova rate and the lack of optically visible supernova detections in the past 400 years. Identifying dust-obscured, missed supernova events via their mid-infrared dust echoes can address this gap.
AI.method: An all-sky, untargeted search was conducted using difference imaging on 12 years of time-resolved NEOWISE co-adds (2009-2022) to detect thermal dust echoes. A convolutional neural network was trained using echo features from Cassiopeia A and archival catalogs to classify transient candidates into dust echoes, point sources, artifacts, and high proper motion stars. The classifier was applied to approximately 11 million transient candidates to identify spatial over-densities of echoes.
AI.result: The model achieved approximately 94% accuracy in distinguishing dust echoes from other sources. Cassiopeia A was the only region exhibiting detectable dust echoes at the WISE sensitivity threshold, consistent with its unique characteristics. A catalog of 20,477 time-resolved echo positions of Cas A within 10 degrees was produced, which is being utilized for interstellar medium studies with the James Webb Space Telescope.
AI.conclusion: This study demonstrates the feasibility of detecting dust-obscured Galactic supernova events via their thermal dust echoes using time-resolved mid-infrared data and machine learning classification. The findings provide a foundation for future higher-sensitivity, higher-resolution surveys with the Roman Space Telescope that will significantly enhance detection capabilities.

authors: E. M. de Gouveia Dal Pino
title: Chasing Gamma-Ray Signals from Binary Neutron Star Coalescences with the Cherenkov Telescope Array: Prospects and Observing Strategies
summary:
The detection of gravitational waves (GWs) from a binary neutron star (BNS) merger by Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo (GW170817), together with its electromagnetic counterpart, the short gamma-ray burst GRB~170817A, heralded the birth of multi-messenger astronomy. The detection of TeV emission from GRBs motivates follow-up observations with the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO), ideal for detecting such signals due to its unprecedented sensitivity, rapid response, and wide-field survey capabilities. The aim of this work is to evaluate GeV--TeV GW follow-up strategies for CTAO using a multi-step simulation pipeline and to estimate the expected rate of joint GW-GRB detections during observing run O5.
  Using a simulated sample of BNS systems with corresponding GW detections, gamma-ray emission is simulated through phenomenological prescriptions based on the observed population of short GRBs, including off-axis jet scenarios. CTAO observations are simulated to account for instrument response, sky tiling strategies, integration times, and varying observing conditions. Strategies with variable and constant integration times are investigated.
  We find that, via an optimized follow-up strategy, about 5% of simulated GW-associated short GRBs produce GeV--TeV radiation detectable by CTAO. Detectability is strongly influenced by the jet opening angle and viewing angle, suggesting that even rough estimates of the viewing angle in GW alerts could enhance targeting. This framework motivates future follow-ups of GW-detectable events, including neutron star-black hole mergers, and further supports the development of advanced strategies incorporating galaxy distributions and synergies with future detectors such as the Einstein Telescope.

AI.tldr: This work simulates and assesses strategies for detecting GeV--TeV emission from short GRBs associated with gravitational wave detections of binary neutron star mergers using CTAO, finding that about 5% can be detected with optimized follow-ups, emphasizing the importance of viewing angle information to improve detection rates.
AI.motivation: The detection of gravitational waves from binary neutron star mergers and associated electromagnetic signals opens new opportunities in multi-messenger astronomy. The recent detection of TeV emission from GRBs motivates the use of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) to follow-up and detect such high-energy signals efficiently.
AI.method: A multi-step simulation pipeline is used to evaluate GeV--TeV GW follow-up strategies for CTAO. Simulated BNS mergers with corresponding GW detections are combined with phenomenological models of gamma-ray emission, including off-axis jet scenarios. CTAO observations are simulated incorporating instrument response, sky tiling, integration times, and observational conditions. Both variable and constant integration time strategies are considered.
AI.result: An optimized follow-up strategy shows that about 5% of simulated GW-associated short GRBs produce GeV--TeV radiation detectable by CTAO. Detectability depends strongly on jet opening and viewing angles, implying that inclusion of viewing angle estimates in GW alerts could improve targeting. The approach supports further follow-up observations and advanced strategies leveraging galaxy distributions and synergy with future detectors.
AI.conclusion: Optimized follow-up observations with CTAO can significantly enhance the rate of detecting high-energy counterparts to GW events from BNS mergers, motivating incorporation of viewing angle information and the development of sophisticated observation strategies to improve joint GW-GRB detections in future observing runs.

title: The Northern High Time Resolution Universe pulsar survey: III. Single-pulse search continuation, follow-up observations, and initial results
summary: We continued the search for single pulses (SPs) in the northern part of the all-sky High Time Resolution Universe survey, whose aim is to detect pulsars and other radio transients. This search is now about 21% complete and has yielded the first discovery of a fast radio burst (FRB) with the 100 m Effelsberg Radio Telescope. FRB20110220A was detected with an S/N-optimised dispersion measure of 501.0 pc/cm$^{3}$ and a width of 11.9 $\pm$ 3.5 ms, for a fluence of 0.6 $\pm$ 0.1 Jy ms. We obtained the first L-band detection of the rotating radio transient (RRAT) J2028+28, from which we obtained upper limits on the source's period and burst rate, as well as an improved position. We also discovered a new RRAT, J0404+53, which had previously been reported as an isolated SP candidate. Eight new SP trains and 272 faint isolated SP candidates were detected too. We used these candidates to demonstrate that their all-sky detection rates depend on Galactic latitude and longitude. This direction dependence suggests the existence of a faint Galactic SP population.

AI.tldr: Using the Effelsberg telescope to search for single pulses, this study discovered a new FRB, detected known and new RRATs, and found that single pulse detection rates vary with Galactic coordinates, implying a faint Galactic transient population.
AI.motivation: To detect pulsars and other radio transients by searching for single pulses in the northern part of the all-sky High Time Resolution Universe survey.
AI.method: Conducting a single pulse search using the 100 m Effelsberg Radio Telescope, analyzing dispersion measures, pulse widths, fluences, and positional data for pulsars, RRATs, and FRBs in the survey data.
AI.result: Discovery of the first fast radio burst (FRB20110220A) with the Effelsberg telescope, first L-band detection of RRAT J2028+28 with improved position and burst rate limits, discovery of a new RRAT J0404+53, detection of eight new single pulse trains and 272 faint isolated single pulse candidates, and identification of directional dependence of single pulse detection rates.
AI.conclusion: The direction-dependent detection rates indicate a faint Galactic single pulse population exists, enhancing the understanding of transient radio source distribution in the Galaxy.

title: Primordial Neutron Stars
summary: We propose a novel cosmological scenario in which baryonic neutron stars could plausibly form in the early universe. If baryogenesis initially produces an excessively-large baryon asymmetry, $Y_B \gg 10^{-10},$ the baryonic mass inside the horizon can exceed the minimum neutron star mass before big bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). While this large asymmetry is present, non-relativistic baryons can dominate the universe and enhanced density perturbations on small scales can gravitationally collapse Hubble patches shortly after horizon re-entry. For some initial perturbations, just below the threshold for black hole formation, this collapse will be arrested only by nuclear pressure, possibly resulting in neutron star formation. Afterwards, there must be a large entropy injection to restore the observed baryon asymmetry, $Y_B \sim 10^{-10}$, and preserve the successful predictions of standard BBN. Unlike neutron stars that form from stellar collapse, primordial neutron stars can, in principle, be as light as $\sim 0.1 M_\odot$, limited only by the nuclear equation of state.

AI.tldr: This paper suggests that if the early universe had a very large baryon asymmetry, small-scale density perturbations could gravitationally collapse and form primordial neutron stars before BBN, with masses potentially as low as 0.1 solar masses, followed by entropy injection to match observed baryon abundances.
AI.motivation: To explore the possibility of neutron star formation in the early universe due to an initially large baryon asymmetry, providing an alternative cosmological scenario.
AI.method: They analyze the implications of a large baryon asymmetry $Y_B \gg 10^{-10}$ causing baryonic mass inside the horizon to exceed the neutron star mass before BBN, leading to gravitational collapse of density perturbations arrested by nuclear pressure.
AI.result: Primordial neutron stars could form shortly after horizon re-entry with masses as low as ~0.1 solar masses, and a subsequent entropy injection restores the observed baryon asymmetry to preserve standard BBN predictions.
AI.conclusion: The paper proposes that baryonic neutron stars could form in the early universe under conditions of large initial baryon asymmetry, resulting in primordial neutron stars of unusually low mass, distinct from those formed by stellar collapse.

title: Radio Monitoring Campaign of Active Repeater FRB 20220912A with CHIME
summary: FRB 20220912A is a highly active repeating fast radio burst (FRB) source, discovered by the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) using its real-time FRB detection system (CHIME/FRB). Here, we present results from a radio monitoring campaign of FRB 20220912A using CHIME, including ~200 hours of data collected by CHIME/Pulsar, spanning 1.5 years following the source's discovery. We present an analysis of a sample of 828 CHIME-detected bursts from FRB 20220912A, in the 400-800 MHz radio frequency band. The source remains highly active for ~10 weeks and has a bimodal wait-time distribution with peaks at $160^{+120}_{-70}$ ms and $306^{+14}_{-13}$ s. Assuming a radio efficiency factor of $10^{-4}$ and a beaming angle of 0.1, we estimate the total emitted energy from the source over the entire observing campaign to be $2 \times 10^{43}$ ergs. We report a 2.3$σ$ detection of a linear increase in the DM of $1.4 \pm 0.6$ pc cm$^{-3}$ yr$^{-1}$, with no significant trend in rotation measure (with a 3$σ$ upper limit of 13.4 rad m$^{-2}$ yr$^{-1}$). We contrast our findings with other active repeaters, which exhibit different DM and RM evolution to indicate that FRB 20220912A may reside in a unique local environment.

AI.tldr: A 1.5-year radio monitoring of FRB 20220912A using CHIME reveals high activity phases, bimodal wait times, significant total energy emission, a slight increase in DM, and unique local environmental conditions distinct from other active repeating FRBs.
AI.motivation: To understand the characteristics, activity, and local environment of the highly active repeating fast radio burst source FRB 20220912A.
AI.method: Conducted a radio monitoring campaign using CHIME/Pulsar over 1.5 years, analyzing ~200 hours of data and a sample of 828 bursts within the 400-800 MHz band.
AI.result: The source shows high activity for ~10 weeks with a bimodal wait-time distribution, a total emitted energy estimated at 2x10^{43} ergs, a weak linear increase in dispersion measure (DM), and no significant rotation measure (RM) trend. Its unique DM and RM evolution suggests a distinct local environment compared to other active repeaters.
AI.conclusion: FRB 20220912A exhibits unique temporal and energetic properties along with distinct DM and RM behavior, implying it resides in a local environment different from other known active repeaters, enhancing the understanding of FRB source environments.

title: FolpsD: combining EFT and phenomenological approaches for joint power spectrum and bispectrum analyses
comment: 42 pages, 19 figures. Supporting paper for the DESI DR2 full-shape key papers
summary: We present a theoretical model for the power spectrum and bispectrum of galaxy clustering that exploits the complementarity between small-scale power spectrum information and large-scale bispectrum measurements. We extend the FOLPS code by combining its one-loop EFT galaxy power spectrum with a tree-level galaxy bispectrum projected onto the tripolar spherical harmonics (Sugiyama) basis. To access additional small-scale information, we also consider a line-of-sight damping factor in both statistics, mirroring approaches commonly used in studies of redshift-space distortions. We test the model using DESI DR2 galaxy mocks. Even without damping, the joint analysis of the EFT power spectrum and bispectrum significantly improves constraints and reduces parameter degeneracies relative to power spectrum analyses alone. For LRG-like samples, including the damping further extends the range beyond $k\sim 0.3 \,h \text{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the power spectrum and $k \sim 0.24 \,h \text{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the bispectrum without introducing statistically significant parameter biases. This leads to up to $\sim 30\%$ tighter constraints on $A_s$ and $ω_{cdm}$. For low signal-to-noise tracers such as QSOs, however, the damping parameters are weakly constrained and can absorb noise fluctuations, leading to shifts in inferred parameters. Similar limitations may arise in models where cosmological information is encoded in power-spectrum shape features degenerate with the damping, such as scenarios with massive neutrinos. In contrast, for $w_0w_a$CDM we obtain $15\%$ and $21\%$ tighter constraints on $w_0$ and $w_a$, respectively, yielding a deviation from constant dark energy at slightly more than the $1σ$ level using full-shape information alone. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/cosmodesi/FolpsD

AI.tldr: This paper enhances galaxy clustering analysis by jointly modeling the power spectrum and bispectrum with an effective field theory approach and damping factors, achieving up to 30% tighter cosmological constraints on DESI DR2 mocks, particularly for dark energy parameters, and provides a publicly available code implementation.
AI.motivation: To improve cosmological parameter constraints by exploiting complementary information from galaxy clustering statistics on different scales, specifically combining small-scale power spectrum data with large-scale bispectrum measurements.
AI.method: Extended the FOLPS code to combine one-loop EFT galaxy power spectrum with tree-level galaxy bispectrum projected onto the Sugiyama tripolar spherical harmonics basis; incorporated a line-of-sight damping factor to access additional small-scale information; tested on DESI DR2 galaxy mocks.
AI.result: Joint analysis of power spectrum and bispectrum improves constraints and reduces parameter degeneracies; inclusion of damping extends analysis to smaller scales without significant bias for LRG-like samples, tightening constraints on parameters like $A_s$ and $\omega_{cdm}$ by up to 30%; for $w_0w_a$CDM model, constraints on dark energy parameters $w_0$ and $w_a$ improved by 15% and 21%, respectively, with slight evidence for deviation from constant dark energy; limitations noted for low signal-to-noise tracers and models with degenerate shapes.
AI.conclusion: The combined approach using power spectrum and bispectrum with damping provides significantly improved and robust cosmological parameter constraints for galaxy clustering data, especially for LRG-like samples, while highlighting potential limitations for noisy tracers and certain cosmological models; the method and code are publicly available for further use.

title: A New Measurement of the Extragalactic Background Light using 15\,yr of {\it Fermi}-Large Area Telescope Data
summary: The extragalactic background Light (EBL) from ultraviolet to infrared comprises the emission from all stars, galaxies, and actively accreting black holes in the observable Universe. A precise measurement of the EBL is critically important to probe models of star formation and galaxy evolution. The EBL can be measured via the absorption imprint left on the spectra of gamma-ray blazars. In this work, we rely on 15 years of {\it Fermi}-LAT data and 1576 blazars to measure the EBL optical depth in the $0<z<4.3$ range. We detect the EBL attenuation with $\sim23σ$ significance and measure the optical depth in 19 redshift bins, extending the coverage and improving on our previous results. This allows us to reconstruct the EBL evolution and find general consistency with recent EBL models. These results represent the most precise determination of the EBL with GeV $γ$ rays to date.

AI.tldr: Using 15 years of Fermi-LAT data from 1576 blazars, this work precisely measures the extragalactic background light's optical depth up to redshift 4.3, detecting attenuation with high significance and confirming agreement with recent models.
AI.motivation: To obtain a precise measurement of the EBL, which is critical for probing models of star formation and galaxy evolution by quantifying the integrated emission of stars, galaxies, and black holes across ultraviolet to infrared wavelengths.
AI.method: The authors analyzed 15 years of Fermi-LAT gamma-ray data from 1576 blazars, detecting EBL attenuation via absorption imprints on blazar spectra across 19 redshift bins within the range 0 to 4.3.
AI.result: Detected EBL attenuation with approximately 23 sigma significance, measured optical depth in 19 redshift bins, reconstructed EBL evolution, and validated consistency with recent theoretical models, representing the most accurate determination of EBL using GeV gamma-ray data to date.
AI.conclusion: The study provides the most precise measurement to date of the extragalactic background light (EBL) optical depth using GeV gamma rays, confirming general consistency with recent EBL models and improving understanding of its evolution up to redshift 4.3.

title: Bounding axion dark energy
summary: We study cosmological solutions of (pseudo)scalar theories with periodic potentials, in the presence of arbitrary cosmological fluids -- including a cosmological constant of either sign. Independently of the initial misalignment angle and field velocity, we derive an analytic bound that the axion mass parameter and decay constant fulfill as the universe decreases its acceleration rate, finding a natural application in models of thawing quintessence. As a first application, we illustrate the analytic handle our bound provides in bounding axion dark energy, after observational inputs from DESI and various supernovae data sets are taken into account. As a second application, we argue that our analytic bounds in combination with proposed quantum gravity constraints on axions exclude vast regions of parameter space. The combined constraints push the axion masses to be much larger than the Hubble scale, in tension with basic models of axion quintessence.

AI.tldr: The paper derives analytic bounds on axion mass and decay constant in cosmological settings, uses observational data and quantum gravity considerations to exclude large parameter regions, challenging simple axion quintessence dark energy models.
AI.motivation: To analyze cosmological solutions of (pseudo)scalar theories with periodic potentials in the presence of various cosmological fluids, aiming to understand constraints on axion parameters in the context of dark energy and quantum gravity.
AI.method: Derivation of an analytic bound relating the axion mass parameter and decay constant, valid independent of initial field conditions, applied to models of thawing quintessence and compared against observational data and quantum gravity constraints.
AI.result: The derived analytic bounds constrain axion dark energy models when combined with observational data from DESI and supernovae, and when combined with quantum gravity constraints, exclude large regions of axion parameter space, pushing axion masses above the Hubble scale and challenging basic axion quintessence models.
AI.conclusion: The combined analytic and observational constraints significantly restrict viable axion quintessence parameter space, implying tensions for simple axion dark energy models with masses below the Hubble scale.

title: The evolution of the mid-infrared spectrum of SN 1987A observed with the JWST/MIRI-MRS
comment: 35 pages, 20 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Supernova (SN) 1987A provides a unique laboratory for investigating many aspects of SN physics and evolution. An observation at Day 12927 (35.4 yr) since the explosion with the Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) Medium Resolution Spectrometer (MRS) on the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) provided the first spatially resolved spectroscopic study of SN 1987A in the mid-IR, yielding insights into the evolution of dust, the ejecta, the equatorial ring (ER), and shocks in the system. Here we present a second epoch with MIRI/MRS at Day 13311 (36.4 yr) allowing the mid-IR spatially resolved spectroscopic temporal evolution of SN 1987A to be probed for the first time. Analysis of the ER-dominated dust continuum showed little evolution between Days 12927 and 13311. However, a spatial analysis reveals the inner ER to be fading while the outermost regions are brightening. Broad ejecta emission lines detected at Day 12927 are evolving rapidly, driven by the recent onset of the ejecta/equatorial ring interaction in the northeast and southwest of the ER. Most lines from the ER show no change during the 384 days between the epochs, though some such as [Ne II] and [Ar II] have faded. We identify mid-IR H2 emission associated with the ejecta for the first time. Using the near- and mid-IR [Fe II] lines as density and temperature diagnostics of the ejecta in the interaction region we find it likely that the dense inner Fe-rich ejecta has now reached the reverse shock. Continued monitoring of SN 1987A is essential to observe the evolving ejecta/ER interaction and dust components.

AI.tldr: Using JWST mid-IR spectroscopy at two epochs ~1 year apart revealed evolving dust and gas interactions in SN 1987A's ejecta and equatorial ring, highlighting dynamic changes and the importance of ongoing observations.
AI.motivation: To investigate the temporal evolution and physical properties of Supernova 1987A and its surrounding components using spatially resolved mid-infrared spectroscopy.
AI.method: Utilizing two epochs of mid-infrared spatially resolved spectroscopic observations of SN 1987A at 35.4 and 36.4 years after the explosion, conducted with the Mid-Infrared Instrument Medium Resolution Spectrometer on the James Webb Space Telescope.
AI.result: The equatorial ring dust continuum showed little overall evolution but spatially varied, with inner regions fading and outer regions brightening. Broad ejecta emission lines evolved rapidly, driven by ejecta/equatorial ring interaction onset. Some emission lines from the ring faded, while mid-IR H2 emission was detected in the ejecta for the first time. Diagnostics indicate the dense Fe-rich ejecta has reached the reverse shock.
AI.conclusion: The temporal evolution of the ejecta and equatorial ring interaction is complex, with spatially varying changes in dust and emission lines indicating ongoing dynamic processes. Continued JWST monitoring is vital to understand these evolving aspects of SN 1987A.

title: The Cosmic Web and Its Filaments: Neutrino Mass from Topology and Persistent Homology
comment: 32 pages, 14 figures, 1 table. Submitted to ApJS (23 Feb 2026); under review
summary: We apply discrete Morse theory, global topology, and persistent homology to characterize the impact of massive neutrinos on the multiscale cosmic web, focusing on filaments. The topology of the cosmic web is sensitive to neutrino imprints, and persistence diagrams provide more information than commonly used summary statistics by quantifying the longevity of topological features across densities. This scale-adaptive, parameter-free formalism is powerful, as massive neutrinos affect halos, walls, filaments, and voids in distinct ways. Within this framework, we simultaneously assess their impact on tracers and skeleton structures and capture their multiscale signals across cosmic time. Discrete Morse theory is also well suited for particle-based neutrino implementations, often affected by Poisson shot noise, as it preserves the salient features of the underlying smooth field. Using two independent sets of N-body simulations, we present filament statistics and persistence diagrams in massive-neutrino cosmologies. Our results show that neutrinos leave distinct imprints on filaments and skeleton connectivity, producing mass-dependent signatures most pronounced at high redshift (z~2) and detectable at the few-percent level for masses as small as $M_ν\sim 0.1$ eV. Filaments thus provide an ideal environment for isolating neutrino effects. We also compare two implementations of massive neutrinos to assess systematics. Our study establishes a promising avenue for leveraging cosmic web topology, persistent homology, and environment-based statistics to constrain or directly detect neutrino mass and infer the mass hierarchy - a long-standing challenge in particle physics and a major objective of ongoing and upcoming galaxy redshift surveys (e.g., DES, DESI, Euclid, Rubin-LSST).

AI.tldr: This paper uses advanced topological methods and simulations to reveal how massive neutrinos uniquely affect cosmic web filaments, enabling novel constraints on neutrino mass and hierarchy, with implications for future galaxy surveys.
AI.motivation: To characterize the impact of massive neutrinos on the multiscale cosmic web and to leverage cosmic web topology for constraining neutrino mass and hierarchy, which is a major challenge in particle physics.
AI.method: Application of discrete Morse theory, global topology, and persistent homology to quantify topological features of cosmic web structures like filaments using two independent sets of N-body simulations, including particle-based neutrino implementations to mitigate Poisson shot noise.
AI.result: Neutrinos leave distinct imprints on filaments and skeleton connectivity with mass-dependent signatures most pronounced at high redshift (z~2), detectable at the few-percent level for neutrino masses as small as ~0.1 eV. Filaments provide an ideal environment to isolate neutrino effects, with systematics assessed via comparison of two neutrino implementations.
AI.conclusion: The cosmic web topology and persistent homology provide a powerful, scale-adaptive, parameter-free framework to detect and constrain neutrino masses and mass hierarchy, establishing a promising method for upcoming galaxy surveys.

title: A TeV-based Determination of the Local Extragalactic Background Light and its Consistency with Galaxy Counts and Direct Measurements
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJL, 12 pages, 6 figures
summary: The extragalactic background light (EBL), the cumulative radiation from all extragalactic sources, traces galaxy formation and cosmic evolution. High-energy $γ$ rays attenuated via pair production with EBL photons are a powerful probe of the EBL. In this work, we use very-high-energy (VHE; $E_γ> 100\,\mathrm{GeV}$) $γ$ rays to measure the local EBL intensity and test its consistency with galaxy counts and direct measurements. Our analysis employs a sample of 268 spectra from 45 sources observed with Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes. A model-dependent study shows seven EBL templates require only $\le 10\%$ rescaling to fit the observed $γ$-ray attenuation. The galaxy-count-anchored model gives the closest match. We then derive template-marginalized TeV optical depths from a representative model subset. We combine them with \textit{Fermi}-LAT GeV measurements to reconstruct the EBL at $z = 0$ using empirical and physically motivated models. The two reconstructions agree and follow the integrated galaxy light to within $2$--$3\,\mathrm{nW\,m^{-2}\,sr^{-1}}$ (typically $<25\%$) over $0.5$--$30\,μ$m. Both are consistent with low-zodiacal-light observations, including outer solar system and dark cloud measurements. In contrast, the near-IR excess reported by IRTS and CIBER exceeds our reconstructed intensity by $3$--$5σ$, implying an additional $\gtrsim 5$--$10\,\mathrm{nW\,m^{-2}\,sr^{-1}}$ incompatible with the $γ$-ray optical depths. Combined with GeV constraints on EBL evolution to $z \simeq 4$, these TeV optical depths provide a VHE-anchored determination of the local EBL intensity. The agreement with galaxy counts and deep-space measurements indicates that known galaxy populations account for most of the optical and near-IR background, leaving limited room for an additional diffuse component.

AI.tldr: Using very-high-energy γ rays from 45 sources, the study accurately reconstructs the local extragalactic background light, confirming it aligns with galaxy counts and deep-space data and challenging reported near-IR excesses, thereby affirming that known galaxies explain most of the optical and near-IR background.
AI.motivation: To measure the local extragalactic background light (EBL) intensity and test its consistency with galaxy counts and direct measurements using very-high-energy (VHE) γ rays.
AI.method: Analysis of 268 spectra from 45 sources observed with Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, employing model-dependent rescaling of seven EBL templates, derivation of template-marginalized TeV optical depths, and combination with Fermi-LAT GeV data to reconstruct the EBL at redshift zero using empirical and physically motivated models.
AI.result: Seven EBL templates require minimal rescaling (≤10%) to fit γ-ray attenuation, the galaxy-count-anchored model fits best, reconstructed EBL intensity matches integrated galaxy light within 2-3 nW m⁻² sr⁻¹, consistent with low-zodiacal-light measurements, and contradicts near-IR excess reported by IRTS and CIBER, implying most optical and near-IR background originates from known galaxies with limited room for additional diffuse components.
AI.conclusion: Known galaxy populations mostly account for the optical and near-infrared extragalactic background light, as confirmed by very-high-energy γ-ray attenuation measurements consistent with galaxy counts and deep-space observations, restricting the presence of an additional diffuse EBL component.

title: Analytic compression of the effective field theory of the Lyman-alpha forest
summary: The 1D flux power spectrum ($P_{\mathrm{1D}}$) of the Ly$α$ forest provides an exceptionally high-resolution probe of structure formation down to small scales ($k\approx1-10~\text{$h~$Mpc$^{-1}$}$). These scales carry the imprints of massive neutrinos, warm dark matter, and the running of the primordial power spectrum spectral index. The effective field theory (EFT) is a promising perturbative approach to systematically and efficiently describe the Ly$α$ forest, but it faces challenges in its application to $P_{\mathrm{1D}}$, as many EFT parameters become degenerate when projected along the line of sight. In addition, this projection generates new stochastic terms from the integration over small-scale modes. In this work, we address these issues by compressing the EFT model space using the Fisher matrix formalism and linearizing the resulting compression directions, enabling analytic template marginalization and significantly reducing the computational cost of likelihood evaluation. We use hydrodynamical simulations to obtain a baseline estimate of EFT parameters, and use the DESI DR1 $P_{\mathrm{1D}}$ measurements to derive compression directions. We then marginalize over deviations from the baseline using these compression directions and forecast the constraining power of our formalism. We find that even in conservative scenarios where each data redshift bin requires its own set of EFT parameters, the cosmological constraints saturate with the linear bias, two leading-order 1D stochastic terms, and three principal combinations of the remaining EFT templates. In this case, our forecasted precision of the amplitude ($Δ^2_p$) and the logarithmic slope ($n_p$) of the linear matter power spectrum at the pivot scale ($k_p=0.7~\text{Mpc}^{-1}$) is $10\%$ and $2.0\%$, respectively, which is similar to emulator-based analyses that include observational data systematics.

AI.tldr: This paper improves effective field theory modeling of the Lyα forest 1D flux power spectrum by compressing parameters and marginalizing analytically, overcoming degeneracies and stochastic projection effects. Using simulations and DESI DR1 data, it forecasts high-precision cosmological constraints comparable to current emulator methods, while reducing computational demands.
AI.motivation: The 1D flux power spectrum of the Lyα forest contains rich cosmological information at small scales, sensitive to effects like massive neutrinos and warm dark matter. However, applying effective field theory (EFT) to this spectrum is challenging due to parameter degeneracies and new stochastic terms from line-of-sight projection.
AI.method: The authors compress the EFT parameter space using Fisher matrix formalism, linearize compression directions for analytic marginalization, and use hydrodynamical simulations plus DESI DR1 data to establish baseline EFT parameters and compression directions. They then marginalize deviations to forecast cosmological parameter constraints.
AI.result: They find that only a limited number of parameters (linear bias, two leading 1D stochastic terms, and three principal EFT combinations) are needed to saturate cosmological constraints across redshift bins. Forecasted precision on the amplitude and slope of the linear matter power spectrum is 10% and 2%, respectively, competitive with emulator-based methods including observational systematics.
AI.conclusion: The developed EFT parameter compression and marginalization approach effectively mitigates degeneracies and stochastic effects in the Lyα forest 1D flux power spectrum analysis, enabling precise cosmological parameter constraints with reduced computational cost, matching or surpassing existing emulator-based analyses.
